newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: MidEast gas oil tightens on exports to East Africa.
newsitem.headline: MidEast gas oil tightens on exports to East Africa.

text.p: Gas oil supplies in the MidEast for lifting in September are tightening as traders looked to that area instead of the Mediterrenean for their sale committments to East Africa, industry sources said on Friday.
Traders said sellers to East Africa have secured their supplies from the MidEast as prices in the Mediterrenean were relatively much higher than that in the MidEast.
As a result, premiums in the MidEast for 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil have risen to about $1.00 per barrel over MidEast spot quotes from about 60 cents per barrel in early August.
The rise in prices aside, it was extremely difficult to secure products for export to Asia as it was more lucrative to export to East Africa, traders said.
Buyers, who are covering their committment to East Africa, are able to pay higher premiums as they are selling these products on a formula that is based on the higher Mediterrenean quotes.
Sources report that several cargoes were already committed for export from the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
